name: Lama (Myanmar)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog: retired entry; 'Lama (lay-lay)' is a name for a section of Nung. No description of a distinct Lama (Myanmar) variety found.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Eric Johnson & Cathryn Yang, SIL East Asia Group). 2013. Change Request Number 2013-007: [lay] 'Lama' -> 'Bai, Lama' (adopted 2014-02-03). Dallas: SIL International. 6 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; identity document only: states Lama [lay] does not exist in Myanmar and is the language of the Lama people (Bai nationality) of Lanping county, Yunnan; renames the code 'Bai, Lama' (Northern Bai / Lan-Bi Bai).

sources.citation: Wang Feng 汪鋒. 2006. Comparison of Languages in Contact: The Distillation Method and the Case of Bai. Language and Linguistics Monograph Series B: Frontiers in Linguistics III. Taipei: Institute of Linguistics, Academia Sinica. xxiv+227 pp. (open access at ILAS).
sources.note: Ch. 2 sect. 2.1 (pp. 31-37) gives phonological systems of Tuoluo (Weixi), Gongxing and Enqi (Lanping) Bai, explicitly identified as the varieties of the Lama 拉瑪 people: syllable = (C)(S)V(C) plus tone; Tuoluo 5 tones (55 33 42 21 35), Gongxing 6 tones, Enqi 5 tones with sandhi. The words 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere in the 260-page book; no statement on word stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record lama1289 'Lama (Myanmar)' (Bookkeeping), with Ethnologue comment: 'a name for a section of Nung [nun] of Nungish branch of Tibeto-Burman (Voegelin & Voegelin 1977:15)'.
Chinese Wikipedia, 拉瑪方言 (Lama dialect of Bai) and 白語 articles; English Wikipedia 'Bai language' and 'Lama language (Bai)'.
sources.note: Nothing on stress; used only to confirm identity ([lay] = Lama Bai of Lanping/Weixi since 2013; before E17 it denoted a purported Nungish language of Myanmar) and to locate Wang Feng's Lama datapoints.

sources.citation: Li Shaoni 李绍尼. 2008. 兰坪拉玛白语概况 [A sketch of Lanping Lama Bai]. In 大理丛书·白语篇 (Dali congshu, Bai language volumes), ed. Xu Lin 徐琳 et al. Kunming: Yunnan Minzu chubanshe.
